verifications.note: Reproduced, then shown fixed. Reproduced: my round-24 suite run against the pre-D-040 round-23 candidate (6438e20) ACCEPTS the exploit. QA24-N1 (the QA23-P1 shape: a self-declared absent round-3, a genuine run whose head holds the manifest but not the fix, and the fix in the gate candidate) and QA24-N2 (the fix committed AFTER the verifier's run started, still in the gate candidate, with the round-3 source_commit forged absent and, separately, genuine) are both ACCEPTED there. Fixed: on candidate f0f3a93a (6db3b83), in a complete --no-local clone, QA24-N1 and QA24-N2 (both variants) are REJECTED with "is not in the verifying run's starting history" as the only non-harness error; the gate-ancestry check does not fire because the fix IS in the gate candidate. The round-23 probe QA23-P1, re-run unchanged, now reports REJECTED. Boundaries are correct: fix == run head and fix a strict ancestor of it are ACCEPTED (QA24-N3); a fix only on the run's side branch is rejected by the gate check alone (QA24-N4); the head can never be a tree id, upper-case, prefix or pre-manifest commit (QA24-N6), so the vhead guard in checkClosure cannot be bypassed. The unit tests 'D-039/D-040 / F-DG0-164/166/246/249' and 'F-DG0-110 / F-DG0-204' pass (62/62). On the complete real history, all 110 CLOSED_VERIFIED fix_revisions are present and ancestors of their verifying run's head_commit_at_start, HEAD and the gate candidate; the dry-run shows no starting-history error. The fix commit 81f036d is an ancestor of this run's head (79fb0f8) and of the candidate (6db3b83).
